title: Atom Builders
subject: physical science
goal: Build atoms and ions from protons, neutrons, and electrons, and explain which number decides the element.
steps: Draw a big circle on scrap paper: the nucleus goes in the middle, electrons around the outside.
Roll for your atom (the table below). Build it: protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons outside.
The Skeptic checks it against the periodic table: the number of protons decides the element.
Roll again. Odd: take away one electron (now it's an ion). Even: add one neutron (now it's another isotope). (Helium-5 and lithium-8 fall apart in under a second: not every isotope is stable.)
The Recorder writes the row: what it is now, protons, neutrons, electrons, mass number, and charge. Take it apart and start again.
listen_for: Counting electrons in the mass number. Ask: where is almost all of an atom's mass?
Thinking a new neutron makes a new element. Ask the Skeptic: did the protons change?
Charge with the sign flipped: one electron taken away makes +1, not −1.
debrief: Ask: which number alone decides the element? How does your table show it?
Ask: carbon-12 and carbon-13 are both carbon. What's the same, and what's different?
sources: Inspired by the build-an-atom idea, also modeled in PhET Interactive Simulations' Build an Atom (University of Colorado Boulder). The activity and questions were written for Paper Loop.
